text:
Kim: PRD draft for the Optimize Toolkit MVP is up: https://redwood.internal/prd/optimize-toolkit-mvp :eyes:
Kim: Asking for focused feedback on acceptance criteria and edge cases. Target ship: internal beta in 6 weeks. Customer asks (AtlasPay) drive some requirements.
Sanjay: skimmed it. good start. can we be explicit about SLOs for latency and cost delta thresholds?
Matt: +1 on SLOs. propose: 95th p50 latency delta <= 15% vs baseline, cost/unit reduction >= 10% for typical convo workloads.
Lisa: AtlasPay asked for deterministic tail latency (99th) for inference <= 350ms for short prompts. that's a hard constraint for them.
Kim: noted. add to acceptance criteria: 99th <= 350ms for seq_len <= 256 on dedicated tier.
Sanjay: acceptance criteria draft suggestion: 
- Functional: batching recommendations produce stable throughput improvements on 3 canonical workloads (chat, completion, embedding).
- Performance: 95th p50 latency change <= 15%, 99th <= customer threshold when configured.
- Cost: measurable token-level cost improvement >= 10% on 2 of 3 workloads with recommended configs.
- Safety: quantization profiles must not degrade generation quality beyond 2% eval score on our regression set.
- Rollout: canary on 5% traffic with automatic rollback on regression.
Matt: add integration tests: 
- end-to-end CI job that runs small sim of 5000 tokens across models and checks latency/cost deltas and output diffs.
- a perf harness job that runs nightly.
Lisa: edge cases to call out: streaming + batching interactions (we should not block streaming pipelines with large batches), tiny requests (<16 tokens) where batching increases latency, long contexts (>= 8k) where KV cache size matters, and pinned session caches for multi-turn chat.
Kim: good list. also privacy/TTL: cached prefixes that contain PII must honor ttl=0 by default, and users can opt-in to higher TTL if they accept compliance notes.
Sanjay: quantify: recommend default KV cache TTL = 0 for user-provided inputs, but enable per-route TTL in console.
Matt: quantization matrix idea: matrix of model family x quant profile -> expected accuracy delta and speedup. include recommended profile per workload.
Lisa: acceptance criteria for quantization: for each recommended profile, provide eval results (perplexity/ROUGE/QA F1) and `diff > threshold -> reject`. keep threshold = 2% relative drop by default.
Kim: scope negotiation: MVP must include 3 user flows: 
1) Console recommendation card for batching/cache/quant with one-click apply to route.
2) CLI tooling to run local sims and produce recommended configs.
3) Telemetry + rollback hooks (metrics are available and can trigger auto-fallback).
Kim: items to push to v2: interactive per-request latency tuning UI, advanced per-model quant tuning, and policy-based multi-variant routing.
Sanjay: customer asks: AtlasPay also wants audit logs for recommendation changes. add to launch criteria (audit trail + perms).
Lisa: and docs: quickstart + troubleshooting guide for user-visible regression. add acceptance criteria: docs covering rollback steps and how to run local sim.
Matt: small config snippet for the CLI/console that I keep referencing: 
```yaml
route: /chat/atlaspay
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_wait_ms: 8
cache:
  prefix_ttl_seconds: 0
  enabled_prefixes: [session_prompt]
quantization:
  profile: q4_0
  allow_quality_degradation: false
```
Kim: that helps. add a note on streaming: when `max_wait_ms > 0` and streaming is enabled, prefer micro-batching with `max_wait_ms <= 8ms` to avoid noticeable streaming delay.
Sanjay: tests for edge-case tiny requests: ensure batching fallback path sets `max_batch_tokens` to avoid grouping > 1 for requests < 16 tokens.
Lisa: Ops/infra ask: include a capacity-simulation tool that estimates GPU utilization given workload histogram. add as non-blocking but strongly recommended for beta.
Kim: prioritization heatmap proposal (quick): must-have: SLOs + canary rollback + audit logs + docs; should-have: CLI sim + console one-click; nice-to-have: capacity simulator + advanced quant tuning UI.
Matt: timeline ask: is 6 weeks realistic if we include CLI sim? maybe 8. recommend split: internal beta in 6 wks (console + telemetry + canary) then CLI sim + audit logs in next release.
Kim: noted. we'll update roadmap to two-phase. who takes ownership of rollout automation? @Sanjay ? (mentioning for visibility)
Sanjay: I can take rollout automation and the canary/rollback hooks.
Lisa: I'll own docs + customer onboarding checklist.
Matt: I'll own the perf harness and the nightly regression jobs.
ci-bot: build:perf-harness #432 passed on main (https://ci.redwood/build/432) :white_check_mark:
Kim: action items summary: 
- Update PRD acceptance criteria with SLOs, cost targets, quant thresholds (Kim)
- Add edge-case list to PRD (Lisa)
- Implement canary + rollback automation (Sanjay)
- Perf harness + CI jobs (Matt)
- Add audit logging requirement for recommendation changes (Kim + Product)
- Split roadmap into beta (6w) + CLI phase (8-10w) (Kim)
Lisa: pinging support: please flag any open questions from AtlasPay, want to align on 99th latency.
Kim: thanks all. will push updated PRD by EOD tomorrow and open a follow-up thread for acceptance sign-off. :thumbsup:
